s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital syndrome with cranial nerve involvement
salient_findings: Left proptosis with resistance to globe retropulsion
Forehead anesthesia in the V1 division of the trigeminal nerve
key_facts: 2-month history of diplopia and pain
Recurring forehead lesion first excised 6 years prior to presentation
Initial histopathologic findings showed a Breslow thickness of 6 mm
Extensive perineural and intraneural invasion
Lesion recurred twice
Visual acuity was 20/20 bilaterally without afferent pupillary defect
Left upper eyelid edema, erythema, and ptosis
Adduction limited on the left with associated strabismus
MRI finding of left superior orbit mass extending to the cavernous sinus
Intense enhancement of the V1 branch of the left frontal nerve with fat stranding

shortlist.label: Malignant melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Recurring forehead lesion with initial histopathologic findings showing a Breslow thickness of 6 mm and extensive perineural and intraneural invasion

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: MRI finding of left superior orbit mass extending to the cavernous sinus

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Intense enhancement of the V1 branch of the left frontal nerve with fat stranding and associated cranial nerve involvement

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion recurred twice with extensive perineural and intraneural invasion, a rare but possible presentation for lymphoma

shortlist.label: Orbital metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of recurring forehead lesion with aggressive features, raising the possibility of metastatic disease

raw.rationale: The patient's history of a recurring forehead lesion with initial histopathologic findings showing a Breslow thickness of 6 mm, extensive perineural and intraneural invasion, and the recent MRI finding of a left superior orbit mass with intense enhancement of the V1 branch of the left frontal nerve, combined with the pathological examination of the frontal nerve biopsy showing malignant cells, all support the diagnosis of malignant melanoma.

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Meningioma typically does not show perineural invasion or originate from a skin lesion

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannoma is a benign tumor that does not typically exhibit malignant features like mitotic activity or extensive invasion

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma would not typically present with a long history of a recurring skin lesion or perineural invasion

rejected.label: Orbital metastasis
rejected.why: While possible, the direct connection to a previous skin lesion and the specific pattern of invasion make malignant melanoma a more direct explanation
